title: Trim Without Buying
goal: Return the middle of the data. One version cannot compile, one allocates, one is free.
hints: The middle already exists inside data - a subslice is just a narrower window onto it.
The dangling version builds a local Vec and tries to return a view into it. The brace wins.
explanation: Sub-slicing a borrow yields a narrower borrow: &data[1..len-1] is pointer arithmetic, zero allocation, lifetime tied to the input by elision. to_vec() copies the middle into a fresh Vec - legitimate only when the caller must own it. The third version is the classic dangling trap: a view into a LOCAL Vec can't leave the function (E0515), no matter how the lifetimes are spelled. Views point at the caller's data or they don't exist.
